units.rhetorical_move: opens by naming the scale, then the aim
units.function: set the crisis size before the modelling aim

original_instantiations: thousands keep moving and more arrive daily
attention falls on integration policies and practices

units.source_excerpt: With thousands of refugees moving across Europe and more arriving each day.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the scale of the movement before naming the aim.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the daily arrival as a measured rate.

units.rhetorical_move: optimizes a named algorithm, then lists the factors
units.function: claim an optimization and then enumerate what was set

original_instantiations: the control variable algorithm gets optimized first
factors cover quality, faith, resources and policy

units.source_excerpt: Firstly, we optimize the Control Variable algorithm to build a model.
units.reusable_pattern: Open with an ordinal, name the algorithm, then list the factors it takes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the optimization as a proven improvement.

units.rhetorical_move: states the finding as a dangling participle
units.function: report the result without a finite main clause

original_instantiations: every factor turns out crucially important
better conditions make movement more likely

units.source_excerpt: Finding out that every factor is of crucial importance.
units.reusable_pattern: Let the finding stand as a participle clause hung on the previous sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read the dangling participle as a finished sentence.

units.rhetorical_move: gives one yearly total and six route shares
units.function: split a single total across named corridors

original_instantiations: one yearly total splits into six named corridors
a monthly ceiling caps the transfer rate

units.source_excerpt: From the optimized Small World Network algorithm, we find a yearly total.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute the split to a named algorithm, then cap it with a monthly rate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume the six shares were derived rather than stated.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the dynamic model applicative
units.function: claim transfer with a nonstandard adjective

original_instantiations: the same model stays applicative once details shift
details need adjusting when parameters turn dynamic

units.source_excerpt: Finding out that our model is also applicative while we should adjust the details.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim the model still applies, then concede that details must change.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct applicative to applicable when quoting this paper.

units.rhetorical_move: closes by asserting the model solves most problems
units.function: end on a broad belief rather than a result

original_instantiations: belief replaces a measured result at the close
most problems are said to be solved

units.source_excerpt: Then we believe that our model can solve most of the problems.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a summary on a belief verb plus an unbounded claim.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the belief as a validated coverage claim.

units.rhetorical_move: repeats the summary opening almost verbatim
units.function: restate the opening so the reader meets it twice

original_instantiations: hundreds of thousands replace the earlier thousands
the same attention sentence returns unchanged

units.source_excerpt: With hundreds of thousands of refugees moving across Europe and more arriving each day.
units.reusable_pattern: Reopen the introduction with the summary sentence, changing only the scale word.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not count the repetition as a second independent finding.

units.rhetorical_move: anchors the background on one dated count
units.function: give one hard number with its date

original_instantiations: applications pass seven hundred thousand by a named month
one country tops the chart on a per-capita rate

units.source_excerpt: By the end of October 2015, European countries had received over 715,000 asylum applications.
units.reusable_pattern: Pin the background to one dated count, then add one country's per-capita rate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the date when reusing the count.

units.rhetorical_move: repeats the summary plan in the same order
units.function: give the reader the plan a second time

original_instantiations: the work section mirrors the summary order exactly
applicable replaces applicative on the second pass

units.source_excerpt: Firstly, we optimize the Control Variable algorithm to build a model to analyze the measures.
units.reusable_pattern: Repeat the summary's ordinal plan, letting one adjective change between the two passes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the two passes into one.

units.rhetorical_move: drops a whole class of countries in four words
units.function: exclude a class with a blunt imperative

original_instantiations: slim refugee countries get ignored outright
few refugees means little influence on the model

units.source_excerpt: Ignore the slim refugees country.
units.reusable_pattern: State an exclusion as a bare imperative, then justify it in the next sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read slim as a defined threshold.

units.rhetorical_move: excludes preparation time, then hedges
units.function: drop a factor and immediately qualify the drop

original_instantiations: preparation time gets ignored as an assumption
the same time returns later as mutual reference

units.source_excerpt: Ignore the time of preparation for transfer.
units.reusable_pattern: Exclude a factor, then say it returns when the sections are compared.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the excluded factor as absent from the whole paper.

units.rhetorical_move: points at the symbol table and stops
units.function: hand the definitions to a table in one line

original_instantiations: one sentence hands every definition to the table
the table caption repeats the instruction

units.source_excerpt: Table 1 shows the definitions of the symbols.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce a notation table with a single pointer sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not expect the pointer sentence to define anything itself.

units.rhetorical_move: splits symbols from their meanings across rows
units.function: let the table detach a symbol from its gloss

original_instantiations: symbols sit in one column and glosses drift
region prints with a gap inside the word

units.source_excerpt: The symbol column and the meaning column do not stay aligned.
units.reusable_pattern: Record a notation table whose rows have come apart.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reconstruct a row the raster does not support.

units.rhetorical_move: motivates each factor by the failure it prevents
units.function: justify a factor through the breakdown it avoids

original_instantiations: weak psychological diathesis leads to breakdown
an unsuitable route lowers the success rate

units.source_excerpt: If refugees do not have great psychological diathesis, they might be breakdown during the movement.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce a factor by describing the failure that follows without it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat might be breakdown as grammatical.

units.rhetorical_move: ranks factors, then asserts the weights
units.function: turn a ranking into coefficients by assertion

original_instantiations: ranks run from one to ten, low to high
weights follow the actual situation by assertion

units.source_excerpt: For the contribution of these five factors, we are in accordance with the actual situation.
units.reusable_pattern: Derive weights by saying they accord with the actual situation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the coefficients as fitted.

units.rhetorical_move: uses a wide comma before the claim
units.function: mark the claim with a full-width comma

original_instantiations: a wide comma stands where a period belongs
the accordance claim follows the wide comma

units.source_excerpt: We rank the four factors of the via countries, with a wide comma.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the full-width comma as part of the sentence rhythm.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not normalize the wide comma to an ASCII comma.

units.rhetorical_move: reads a figure aloud in rank order
units.function: turn a plot into a spoken ranking

original_instantiations: physical quality ranks first and literacy third
choice ability comes fourth in the spoken order

units.source_excerpt: The physical quality is the first, mentally quality is the second.
units.reusable_pattern: Read a parameter figure aloud as an ordinal ranking.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct mentally quality when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: gates transfer on matching religion
units.function: make religion a hard on-off gate

original_instantiations: matching religion opens the transfer gate
different religion closes the gate entirely

units.source_excerpt: Flag whether country i and country j have the same religion.
units.reusable_pattern: Treat shared religion as a gate that is either open or shut.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the gate into a weight.

units.rhetorical_move: assigns two mortalities by route type
units.function: split mortality into water and land

original_instantiations: water routes carry the higher mortality
land routes carry the smaller mortality

units.source_excerpt: The mortality differs between a water route and a land route.
units.reusable_pattern: Give mortality as two rates, one per route type.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the two rates into one average.

units.rhetorical_move: reports a monthly average from old data
units.function: state the cap and the years it came from

original_instantiations: the monthly average comes from two named years
the same average becomes the transfer cap

units.source_excerpt: As reached from the 2004's and 2005's data, the average result is a monthly rate.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute a monthly cap to two named data years.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not update the data years.

units.rhetorical_move: credits the graph to a named tool
units.function: name the software that drew the figure

original_instantiations: the transfer graph comes from a named tool
the tool is named in lowercase

units.source_excerpt: We show the transfer graph with the help of pajek.
units.reusable_pattern: Credit a figure to its tool in a short with-the-help-of clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not capitalize the tool name when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: lets capacity fall by arrivals
units.function: update capacity by subtracting what arrived

original_instantiations: capacity this period equals the start minus arrivals
arrivals reduce what the country can still hold

units.source_excerpt: The capacity falls by the refugees already received.
units.reusable_pattern: Write the capacity update as a starting value minus arrivals.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reverse the subtraction.

units.rhetorical_move: says belief reforms gradually for necessity
units.function: let a belief term change because it must

original_instantiations: belief reforms gradually because necessity demands it
the reform is stated, not derived

units.source_excerpt: The belief is reformed gradually for necessity.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a changing belief by necessity alone.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not supply a mechanism the text does not give.

units.rhetorical_move: floors the habit penalty at zero
units.function: keep a penalty from going negative

original_instantiations: great conflict draws a small habit penalty
the penalty is floored so it cannot fall below zero

units.source_excerpt: The habit term is a small penalty on great conflict and zero otherwise.
units.reusable_pattern: Define a habit penalty that is floored at zero.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let the penalty stack without the floor.

units.rhetorical_move: makes any great conflict a hard law flag
units.function: turn conflict into a binary legal block

original_instantiations: any great conflict sets the law flag to zero
no conflict leaves the law flag at one

units.source_excerpt: The law term is zero on any great conflict and one otherwise.
units.reusable_pattern: Encode legal conflict as a flag that is zero or one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not grade the flag into more than two values.

units.rhetorical_move: lets one war zero a whole route
units.function: show one event collapsing one route

original_instantiations: one war closes a route completely
the saturation on that route drops to zero at once

units.source_excerpt: One war completely closed a route and the saturation can instantly drop to zero.
units.reusable_pattern: Show an exogenous event driving one route's saturation to zero.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not spread the zero across every route.

units.rhetorical_move: judges the fit with a hedged phrase
units.function: claim agreement and hedge it in the same clause

original_instantiations: the model fits the events by the large
adjusting parameters would solve it more perfectly

units.source_excerpt: Our model fit the occurrence of exogenous events by the large.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim a fit with a hedged adverb, then promise a better one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read by the large as a statistical term.

units.rhetorical_move: says enlarging the size still satisfies the model
units.function: claim scale invariance, then retract it

original_instantiations: a larger refugee size still satisfies the model overall
the same size then becomes the major subject

units.source_excerpt: If the size of refugees is enlarged, our model can be satisfied overall.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim the model survives a larger scale, then make scale the new subject.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not keep both claims without the retraction.

units.rhetorical_move: bounds stability by a multiple of the scale
units.function: give the scale at which stability holds and fails

original_instantiations: stability holds when the scale stays below ten times
stability weakens once the scale reaches fifteen times

units.source_excerpt: The model is in point when the scale is less than ten times.
units.reusable_pattern: State stability as holding below one multiple and weakening at a larger one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a value between the two multiples.

units.rhetorical_move: credits the computation to MATLAB
units.function: name the tool that produced the numbers

original_instantiations: the matrix is calculated with the help of MATLAB
the tool name appears in capitals

units.source_excerpt: With the help of MATLAB, we can calculate the matrix.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute a numeric result to MATLAB in a fronted with-the-help-of clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge this credit with the pajek credit.

units.rhetorical_move: misspells a parameter in a caption
units.function: leave the caption typo in place

original_instantiations: the caption spells parameter without the second a
the same misspelling labels more than one figure

units.source_excerpt: Figure 9 Different paremeter.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a repeated caption typo as evidence of one hand.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the caption when citing it.

units.rhetorical_move: claims wide applicability from reasonable results
units.function: argue from a reasonable result to a wide range

original_instantiations: results turn out reasonable, so the model is reliable
applicability is said to cover most refugee fields

units.source_excerpt: The results turn out to be reasonable, so our model is practical and reliable.
units.reusable_pattern: Move from results called reasonable to a claim of wide applicability.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat reasonable as a measured error.

units.rhetorical_move: adds one criterion and reports a small change
units.function: test sensitivity by inserting one extra factor

original_instantiations: preparation time enters as one new criterion
relative influence barely changes after the insertion

units.source_excerpt: Every weighted incidence degree changes a little after adding the time of preparation.
units.reusable_pattern: Test sensitivity by adding one criterion and reporting a small change.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the change as zero.

units.rhetorical_move: circulates the calculation to claim stability
units.function: repeat the computation and call that stability

original_instantiations: the calculation is circulated to ensure stability
every object is weighed by its incidence degree

units.source_excerpt: We circulate the calculation process and weigh every evaluation object.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim stability from running the same calculation again.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read circulate as a formal iteration scheme.

units.rhetorical_move: promotes the model to other fields
units.function: claim wider reliability by leaving the original area

original_instantiations: the model is promoted beyond a single area
wider application is said to raise reliability

units.source_excerpt: We promote the model to different fields rather than keep it in one area.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim reliability from applying the model outside its original field.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the other fields, since the text does not.

units.rhetorical_move: blames inaccurate data on limited resources
units.function: admit error and name its cause

original_instantiations: data is sometimes not accurate enough
limited resources and weak technique cause the error

units.source_excerpt: Sometimes it is not accurate enough due to the limitations of resources.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit an inaccuracy and attribute it to scarce resources.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not quantify the error, since no magnitude is given.

units.rhetorical_move: says the full diagram would be disordered
units.function: justify an incomplete figure by its clutter

original_instantiations: too many objects would disorder the diagram
schematic diagrams stand in for the full one

units.source_excerpt: The transfer diagram would be rather disordered if all the objects were included.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a partial diagram by saying the full one would be disordered.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reconstruct the omitted objects.

units.rhetorical_move: reports scores that cluster together
units.function: admit the results fail to separate

original_instantiations: many evaluation objects score close together
the clustering lowers the persuasion of the results

units.source_excerpt: The results of many evaluation objects are close, lowering the persuasion.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit that clustered scores weaken the result's persuasion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a separation the text does not show.

units.rhetorical_move: prints one author name with a stray comma
units.function: keep a citation's typo as part of the voice

original_instantiations: one author name carries a stray comma
the citation otherwise follows a journal format

units.source_excerpt: James Hollifield, Philip Martin, Pia Orrenius, with a wide comma.
units.reusable_pattern: Leave a citation's stray wide comma unrepaired.
prohibited_generalizations: The citation belongs to this reference list and does not transfer.

units.rhetorical_move: opens the letter with a pleasure formula
units.function: raise the register for the policy letter

original_instantiations: pleasure opens the letter to the unnamed reader
the advice is framed as a policy recommendation

units.source_excerpt: It is my pleasure to give policy recommendation to UN.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a policy letter with a pleasure formula addressed to an institution.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a signatory name the letter does not give.

units.rhetorical_move: gives three advices in ordinal order
units.function: turn results into three numbered recommendations

original_instantiations: cultural match comes first among the advices
a buffer zone comes second and doctors third

units.source_excerpt: Firstly, we suggest that give priority to the cultural restraint and religion.
units.reusable_pattern: Deliver policy as three ordinal advices, each one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth advice.

units.rhetorical_move: closes the letter on a hope
units.function: end the letter with a wish for the refugees

original_instantiations: the close hopes the advice helps refugees through
tough days names the hardship without detail

units.source_excerpt: We hope it sincerely that the advice can help refugees to come through the tough days.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a policy letter on a hope verb and a hardship phrase.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read the hope as a measured outcome.
